short: Run coding agents on Agent Substrate, in your organization's cluster
long:
Run Claude Code, Codex and other coding agents in a Kubernetes cluster that runs
Agent Substrate, with DefenseClaw guarding every tool call, model call and network
request the same way it does on a laptop. The agent works on a copy of your folder
inside a sandbox in the cluster; no keys are in it. It keeps running when you
detach, and you can come back from any machine.

Sign in once with "defenseclaw substrate login", then run "defenseclaw substrate run claude"
in a project folder. These commands need no local DefenseClaw install.

short: List what your agents are waiting for you to approve
long:
Lists the questions your agents asked that nobody has answered yet. Answer with
"defenseclaw substrate approve ID" or "defenseclaw substrate reject ID". An agent attached to your
terminal shows the same question on its last line. An unattended run (--task) never waits:
its asks are denied.

short: Send a signed policy bundle to the cluster, or see what is in force (administrators)
long:
A policy bundle is a signed file your organization's policy tooling makes. Administrators send it to the cluster
with "bundle apply" and read which bundles are in force with "bundle status". The cluster checks the signature; this
command only sends the file as it is.

short: Send a signed policy bundle to the cluster
long:
Sends the bundle file to the cluster as it is (up to 32 MiB). With --atespaces the bundle applies to those groups
of agents only; without it, to the whole cluster. With --dry-run it only checks that the file can be read and is not
empty, and sends nothing. Needs an administrator sign-in.
example:
defenseclaw substrate bundle apply policy.bundle
defenseclaw substrate bundle apply policy.bundle --atespaces team-a,team-b --dry-run

short: Check that this computer can run agents in the cluster
long:
Checks, from this computer, everything a run needs: the cluster is set up here, its admin address answers
over TLS, you are signed in and the cluster accepts it, the sign-in server matches, the agent entrance answers over TLS and
you have what it asks for, and your sign-in can be kept safely. Nothing needs to be installed here, and nothing in the
cluster changes.

Administrators get the cluster's own checks too (version, issuer, snapshot bucket, access policies, egress callout, router
clients, routes, API access). They run by themselves when the cluster offers them; --cluster shows why when it does not.

The last line is "ready for agents" when no check failed. Otherwise it is "not ready" and each failed check says how to fix
it, and the exit code is 1.
example:
defenseclaw substrate doctor
defenseclaw substrate doctor --cluster --json

short: Sign in to a cluster
long:
Signs you in to the cluster your organization runs, with your own account. It prints a web
address and a short code; open the address in any browser, enter the code and approve. Your
sign-in is kept in the system keychain, never in a file you can read. The first time, give the cluster's
addresses (your administrator has them); after that, "defenseclaw substrate login" alone renews the sign-in.

In CI, use --workload (or set DEFENSECLAW_SUBSTRATE_WORKLOAD_TOKEN_FILE): the run is then attributed to the
pipeline's own identity, with a GitHub Actions or Kubernetes service-account token, and nothing is stored.
example:
defenseclaw substrate login --admin-url https://admin.example.test:9443 --issuer https://sso.example.test/realms/corp --client-id defenseclaw-launcher
defenseclaw substrate login
defenseclaw substrate login --workload --workload-token-file /var/run/secrets/ci/token

short: Run a coding agent in the cluster on a copy of this folder
long:
Starts the coding agent in a sandbox in the cluster, on a copy of the current folder (secret
files such as .env and keys are held back), and puts the agent on your terminal. The agent is claude,
codex, copilot, opencode, kiro, hermes or antigravity (amp, cursor-agent and devin are not verified yet, so
they do not run). A banner shows the guard profile, model, allowed hosts and how to leave. Questions the
guard asks appear on the last line: [o]nce [a]lways [d]eny.

Press Ctrl-] to detach; the agent keeps running and suspends when idle. Come back from any machine with
"defenseclaw substrate connect NAME". Bring the changes home with "defenseclaw substrate pull NAME".

With --task the agent runs headless without you: asks are denied and the run is checked as strictly as
an unattended job. Add --detach to leave it running and follow it with "defenseclaw substrate logs -f NAME".
With --batch FILE every task gets its own agent on the same folder; --parallel limits how many run at once.
With --clone URL the agent starts from a repository instead of a copy of the folder. Arguments after -- go
to the agent.
example:
defenseclaw substrate run claude
defenseclaw substrate run codex --task "fix the failing tests" --detach
defenseclaw substrate run claude --batch tasks.yaml --parallel 5
defenseclaw substrate run claude --clone https://git.example.test/team/app.git

short: Add DefenseClaw's settings to the SubstrateInstall file (administrators)
long:
Reads the SubstrateInstall document you give to ate-setup and adds the settings DefenseClaw needs: the egress
callout, the router client the gateway attaches launchers through, and, only when you say your Substrate build has them,
the callout body opt-in and the long-stream timeouts. It refuses when Substrate already sends egress to another callout,
and says what to do. Nothing here contacts the cluster.

The result is written next to the file as FILE.new (mode 0600) for you to read. With --yes it replaces the file and keeps
the old one as FILE.bak. With --dry-run it only shows the changes. With --remove it takes DefenseClaw's settings out again.

With --print-access-policies and --plan FILE it prints the access policies the install would write, as commands and
manifests a global owner can apply, and reads no install file.

Next: run ate-setup deploy with the new file, then install the chart with helm install.
example:
defenseclaw substrate setup --install-file install.yaml --namespace defenseclaw --dry-run
defenseclaw substrate setup --install-file install.yaml --capability route-timeouts --yes
defenseclaw substrate setup --print-access-policies --plan plan.json

short: Build, check and publish actor images with their attestation (administrators)
long:
Administrators build the images agents run in, check that an image would be admitted, scan one, publish it to the
registry the cluster pulls from, and make the signing key. These commands run on this computer and need no sign-in.

  build     build an image from a base image and push it with its attestation
  verify    check an image's attestation
  scan      scan an image
  publish   copy a verified image to the cluster's registry
  keygen    make a signing key pair

Run defenseclaw substrate template COMMAND --help for the flags.

short: Build an actor image from a base image and push it with its attestation
long:
Builds a coding-agent image for the cluster from a base image: adds the DefenseClaw hook and relay, scans what is
inside, and pushes it with a signed attestation that the cluster checks before it runs the image.

Usage: defenseclaw substrate template build --from IMAGE --to REPO:TAG --hook-binary FILE --relay-binary FILE --key FILE [flags]

Flags:
  --connector NAME                claudecode or codex (default claudecode)
  --from IMAGE                    base image (the OpenShell harness image for the connector, with tmux)
  --to REPO:TAG                   target repository and tag
  --kit-version VERSION           kit version (default dev)
  --hook-binary FILE              defenseclaw-actor-hook (linux static)
  --relay-binary FILE             defenseclaw-actor-relay (linux static)
  --key FILE                      attestation private key (PEM, mode 0600); not needed with --dry-run
  --anchors FILE                  trust anchors, to let an attested base count as trusted
  --allow-unverified-base         build on a base that is not trusted (the cluster will refuse it by default)
  --block-at LEVEL                lowest finding severity that blocks the build: critical, high, medium, low or none (default high)
  --policy-generation N           policy generation recorded in the attestation (default 1)
  --builder-id ID                 builder id recorded in the attestation
  --provider NAME                 model route (claudecode: bedrock or anthropic; codex: openai or bedrock-mantle)
  --model ID                      default model id
  --gateway-url URL               actor listener URL (default the in-cluster Service)
  --fail-mode MODE                interactive outage mode: open or closed
  --no-mcp-static                 do not run mcp-scanner over tool descriptions
  --mcp-analyzers LIST            mcp-scanner analyzers (default yara)
  --keep-entrypoint               keep the base image ENTRYPOINT and CMD (tests; a real actor image starts the relay)
  --dry-run                       scan the composed image and stop before pushing
  --trusted-base sha256:DIGEST    base image digest the admin trusts (repeatable)
  --mcp-host HOST                 remote MCP host that is allowed (repeatable)
  --session-key KID=FILE          relay session public key, kid=PEM file (repeatable)

Flags build, verify, scan and publish all take:
  --json                          print JSON
  --insecure-registry HOST:PORT   registry reached over plain HTTP (repeatable)
  --registry-user USER            registry user
  --registry-password-file FILE   file with the registry password
  --config FILE                   DefenseClaw config.yaml (scanner and admission settings)
  --platform OS/ARCH              image platform (default linux/amd64)

Exit code: 0 built, 1 blocked, 2 usage error.
example: defenseclaw substrate template build --connector claudecode --from REGISTRY/base:TAG --to REGISTRY/actor:TAG --hook-binary hook --relay-binary relay --key attestation.key

short: Make a signing key pair for attestations
long:
Makes a signing key pair for attestations: attestation.key (private, mode 0600; keep it in the cluster Secret) and
attestation.pub (the trust anchor).

Usage: defenseclaw substrate template keygen --out DIR [flags]

Flags:
  --out DIR                       directory for attestation.key and attestation.pub; required
  --json                          print JSON

Exit code: 0 done, 2 usage error.

short: Copy a verified image to the cluster's registry
long:
Copies a verified image, and its attestation, to the registry the cluster pulls from. It verifies first and refuses an
image that would not be admitted.

Usage: defenseclaw substrate template publish SOURCE@DIGEST TARGET:TAG --anchors FILE [flags]

Flags:
  --anchors FILE                  trust anchors (PEM bundle of public keys); required
  --min-policy-generation N       refuse attestations scanned under an older policy generation (default 0)

Flags build, verify, scan and publish all take:
  --json                          print JSON
  --insecure-registry HOST:PORT   registry reached over plain HTTP (repeatable)
  --registry-user USER            registry user
  --registry-password-file FILE   file with the registry password
  --config FILE                   DefenseClaw config.yaml (scanner and admission settings)
  --platform OS/ARCH              image platform (default linux/amd64)

Exit code: 0 published, 1 not published, 2 usage error.
example: defenseclaw substrate template publish SOURCE@sha256:DIGEST TARGET:TAG --anchors attestation.pub

short: Scan an image for risky skills, MCP servers and plugins
long:
Scans an image the way a build does (skills, MCP servers, plugins and the hook files) and prints the verdict. It
changes nothing.

Usage: defenseclaw substrate template scan IMAGE [flags]

Flags:
  --no-mcp-static                 do not run mcp-scanner over tool descriptions
  --mcp-analyzers LIST            mcp-scanner analyzers (default yara)
  --block-at LEVEL                lowest finding severity that blocks: critical, high, medium, low or none (default high)
  --connector NAME                check the kit's hook files and switches for this connector (claudecode or codex)
  --mcp-host HOST                 remote MCP host that is allowed (repeatable)

Flags build, verify, scan and publish all take:
  --json                          print JSON
  --insecure-registry HOST:PORT   registry reached over plain HTTP (repeatable)
  --registry-user USER            registry user
  --registry-password-file FILE   file with the registry password
  --config FILE                   DefenseClaw config.yaml (scanner and admission settings)
  --platform OS/ARCH              image platform (default linux/amd64)

Exit code: 0 clean, 1 blocked, 2 usage error.
example: defenseclaw substrate template scan REGISTRY/actor@sha256:DIGEST --connector claudecode

short: Check an image's attestation the way the cluster does
long:
Checks the attestation of an image the way the cluster does, and says whether it would be admitted.

Usage: defenseclaw substrate template verify IMAGE --anchors FILE [flags]

Flags:
  --anchors FILE                  trust anchors (PEM bundle of public keys); required
  --min-policy-generation N       refuse attestations scanned under an older policy generation (default 0)
  --max-age DURATION              refuse attestations older than this, for example 720h (default 0, no limit)
  --allow-unverified-base         admit a template built on an untrusted base
  --allow-tag                     accept a tag reference (it can move; pin by digest in templates)
  --revoke KEYID                  key id to refuse (repeatable)

Flags build, verify, scan and publish all take:
  --json                          print JSON
  --insecure-registry HOST:PORT   registry reached over plain HTTP (repeatable)
  --registry-user USER            registry user
  --registry-password-file FILE   file with the registry password
  --config FILE                   DefenseClaw config.yaml (scanner and admission settings)
  --platform OS/ARCH              image platform (default linux/amd64)

Exit code: 0 admitted, 1 not admitted, 2 usage error.
example: defenseclaw substrate template verify REGISTRY/actor@sha256:DIGEST --anchors attestation.pub
